facts.text: Gardena earned the nickname “Freeway City” because the Artesia, Harbor, and San Diego freeways border it on three sides.
In 1911 the Japanese Association opened the Moneta Japanese Institute, and the Gardena Japanese School followed in 1916, marking early Japanese community roots.
The Satow building, dedicated February 26, 1977, honors a prominent Japanese American who helped shape Gardena’s cultural landscape.
Before becoming a city, Gardena was known as the berry‑growing capital of southern California, a fact still celebrated by locals.
Olympic gold‑medalist Lisa Leslie was born in Gardena, and the city also counts Tyga, who attended Gardena High School, among its famous residents.
